name: Russia
description: The largest country on Earth by area, stretching across eleven time zones from the Baltic to the Pacific. It holds Lake Baikal, the deepest lake on the planet, along with the endless taiga and tundra of Siberia.
fact: The Trans-Siberian Railway, the longest railway line in the world, runs across Russia.

name: United States
description: Fifty states with wildly different climates and ways of life, from the skyscrapers of New York to the canyons of Arizona and the studio lots of Los Angeles. Jazz, blues and rock and roll all started here and spread across the world.
fact: The Statue of Liberty in New York was a gift to the United States from France in the late 19th century.

name: China
description: One of the oldest civilisations in the world, which gave humanity paper, gunpowder and silk. The Great Wall runs for thousands of kilometres, and megacities like Shanghai sit alongside centuries-old tea ceremony traditions.
fact: China was the most populous country in the world for nearly all of recorded history, until India recently overtook it.

name: Japan
description: An island nation where ancient Shinto shrines stand a short walk from neon-lit Tokyo streets and shinkansen bullet trains. Japanese food, from sushi to ramen, and traditions like origami are known everywhere.
fact: Mount Fuji, a sacred volcano in Japan, draws hundreds of thousands of hikers and pilgrims every year.

name: Germany
description: The birthplace of Bach, Beethoven and Brahms, and of car brands like BMW and Mercedes-Benz. Medieval Bavarian castles sit at one end of the country, the industrial might of the Ruhr at the other.
fact: Oktoberfest in Munich is the largest beer festival in the world, drawing millions of visitors every year.

name: France
description: The home of haute couture, wine and one of the most influential cuisines in the world, whose dishes and sauces became the foundation of restaurant cooking. The Eiffel Tower and the Louvre draw millions of visitors to Paris each year.
fact: The baguette and other traditional French breadmaking have been added to UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage.

name: Italy
description: The cradle of the Roman Empire and the Renaissance, where Michelangelo and Leonardo da Vinci made some of the world's greatest art. Pizza, pasta and espresso all come from here, and the boot-shaped peninsula is packed with UNESCO sites.
fact: Italy contains the Vatican, a separate state entirely surrounded by the city of Rome.

name: Spain
description: A country of flamenco, bullfighting and the afternoon siesta, and the origin of paella and tapas. Antoni Gaudí's architecture in Barcelona and the Moorish legacy of Andalusia make it one of the most visited countries in Europe.
fact: Spain is the second-largest country in the European Union by area, after France.

name: United Kingdom
description: An island kingdom that gave the world football, The Beatles and afternoon tea. Big Ben in London, the Scottish Highlands and the castles of Wales reflect the variety of its four historic nations.
fact: The United Kingdom is made up of four parts: England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

name: Portugal
description: A nation of navigators from the Age of Discovery, whose caravels reached India and Brazil. Fado, the melancholy songs sung to a guitar, and port wine from the Douro Valley became its calling cards.
fact: Portugal is considered one of the oldest countries in Europe, with borders that have barely changed for centuries.

name: Netherlands
description: A country of canals, tulips and windmills, much of it reclaimed from the sea with dikes and polders. Amsterdam is famous for its cycling culture and for the paintings of Rembrandt and Van Gogh.
fact: About a quarter of the Netherlands lies below sea level, and roughly half of it rises less than a metre above it.

name: Belgium
description: A small country famous for chocolate, waffles and hundreds of varieties of beer, as well as for the comics that gave us Tintin and the Smurfs. Brussels hosts the headquarters of both the European Union and NATO.
fact: Belgians consider their country the birthplace of fries, even though many languages still call them "French".

name: Switzerland
description: A mountain country famous for precision watchmaking, chocolate and cheese full of holes. The Alpine slopes draw skiers and climbers, and Switzerland has kept its neutral status for more than two centuries.
fact: Switzerland has four official languages: German, French, Italian and Romansh.

name: Austria
description: An Alpine country with an extraordinary musical legacy: Mozart, Haydn and Strauss all worked here. Viennese coffee houses, Schönbrunn Palace and the snowy ski resorts of Tyrol define how it looks and feels.
fact: The Viennese ball and the waltz that goes with it are an inseparable part of Austrian cultural identity.

name: Sweden
description: A Scandinavian country of thousands of lakes and islands that gave the world ABBA, IKEA furniture and fika, the habit of pausing for coffee and something sweet. Stockholm is built across fourteen islands.
fact: The three-point seat belt, now standard in every car in the world, was designed by engineers at Sweden's Volvo.

name: Norway
description: The land of the fjords, narrow arms of sea cut between high cliffs, and the home of skiing and Viking legend. Above the Arctic Circle the northern lights show up in the winter sky.
fact: Norwegians were among the first to use skis for everyday travel, and the English word "ski" comes from Norwegian.

name: Finland
description: A country of a thousand lakes and thick forests where the sauna is not a luxury but part of daily life for almost every family. Finland gave the world Nokia and the Moomins, and regularly tops the rankings of the happiest countries.
fact: Finland has more saunas than cars, with one in nearly every house and apartment.

name: Denmark
description: A Scandinavian kingdom that gave the world LEGO bricks and the fairy tales of Hans Christian Andersen. Danes were among the first anywhere to make the bicycle their main way of getting around town.
fact: Denmark is one of the oldest monarchies in the world, with an unbroken line of ruling monarchs.

name: Iceland
description: An island of volcanoes, geysers and glaciers, where hot springs sit beside harsh fields of lava. Despite the name, Iceland is known less for ice than for the geothermal energy that heats almost every home.
fact: Iceland has almost no forests, and the legend of the hidden people, elves living among the rocks, is still alive.

name: Ireland
description: The Emerald Isle, green in a hundred shades, famous for its pubs, its traditional music and its love of a good story. Guinness comes from here, as does St Patrick's Day, now celebrated all over the world.
fact: The shamrock is a national symbol of Ireland and is tied to the legend of St Patrick.

name: Poland
description: A country with a long history and a medieval old town in Warsaw, rebuilt after the war and now on the UNESCO list. Chopin and Marie Skłodowska-Curie were born here, and Polish pierogi are known far beyond its borders.
fact: St Mary's Church in Kraków is known for its trumpeter, who plays a tune every hour that breaks off abruptly halfway through.

name: Czech Republic
description: A country of medieval castles and breweries, where people drink more beer per head than anywhere else in the world. Prague, with Charles Bridge and the castle above the river, is considered one of Europe's most beautiful cities.
fact: The word "robot" comes from Czech, first used by the writer Karel Čapek in a play from 1920.

name: Hungary
description: A country on the Danube, famous for the thermal baths of Budapest and for paprika-heavy goulash. Hungarian is unlike any of its neighbours' languages, and the fiery csárdás and the music of Franz Liszt are matters of national pride.
fact: Budapest was created in the late 19th century by merging three towns: Buda, Pest and Óbuda.

name: Greece
description: The cradle of European philosophy, theatre and the Olympic Games, and the place that gave the world democracy as a form of government. The whitewashed houses of Santorini and the ruins of the Acropolis draw millions of visitors a year.
fact: Greece has several thousand islands, but only around two hundred of them are permanently inhabited.

name: Turkey
description: A country spread across two continents, Europe and Asia, divided by the Bosphorus strait running through Istanbul. Byzantine and Ottoman heritage, endless glasses of tea and a generous idea of hospitality all meet here.
fact: Turkey grows most of the world's hazelnuts, which end up in chocolate factories around the globe.

name: Croatia
description: A ragged Adriatic coastline with a thousand islands, and the old walled city of Dubrovnik behind its massive fortifications. Croatia is considered the birthplace of the necktie, whose name comes from the French word for Croats.
fact: Plitvice Lakes National Park is famous for the cascades of turquoise waterfalls linking its sixteen lakes.

name: Serbia
description: A Balkan country where the Danube meets the Sava, known for its loud brass-band festivals and for the Kalemegdan fortress in Belgrade. Serbian cooking leans on the grill and on Turkish and Austro-Hungarian influences.
fact: Novak Djokovic, one of the greatest tennis players in history, comes from Belgrade.

name: Montenegro
description: A small Balkan country where the mountains drop almost sheer into the Adriatic. Medieval Kotor, ringed by walls at the head of a narrow bay, is one of the most recognisable sights in the country.
fact: The country's name means "black mountain", after a range covered in dark forest.

name: Bulgaria
description: A Balkan country of rose plantations in the Kazanlak valley, which supply rose oil to perfume makers all over the world. Bulgarian yoghurt and its winemaking traditions go back to ancient Thracian times.
fact: The Cyrillic alphabet, used in Russia and other countries, was created and developed in medieval Bulgaria.

name: Romania
description: A country of the Carpathian mountains and Transylvania, tied in the popular imagination to Count Dracula and Bran Castle. Romanian kept its Latin roots while surrounded by Slavic languages and Hungarian.
fact: Bran Castle in Transylvania is often linked to the Dracula legend, though the historical connection is thin.

name: Ukraine
description: The largest country entirely within Europe, with fertile black-earth steppes that have fed much of the continent for generations. The Kyiv Pechersk Lavra and the embroidered vyshyvanka shirt belong to centuries of cultural heritage.
fact: UNESCO has added the Ukrainian culture of cooking borscht to its list of intangible cultural heritage.

name: Belarus
description: A country of thousands of lakes and vast forests, including Belovezhskaya Pushcha, one of the last stretches of primeval woodland in Europe and home to wild bison. Minsk was rebuilt almost from scratch after the war and is known for its broad avenues.
fact: Belovezhskaya Pushcha holds one of Europe's largest herds of wisent, which returned after nearly dying out.

name: Georgia
description: A Caucasian country with one of the oldest winemaking traditions in the world, where wine is still aged in clay vessels called qvevri. The mountain scenery of Svaneti, plus khinkali and khachapuri, have made it a favourite with food travellers.
fact: Georgian qvevri winemaking is recognised by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage.

name: Armenia
description: One of the oldest Christian countries in the world, where monasteries more than a thousand years old stand against the snowy backdrop of Mount Ararat. Armenian brandy and a table laid generously for guests are known well beyond the Caucasus.
fact: Armenia adopted Christianity as its state religion in the early 4th century, among the first countries in the world.

name: Azerbaijan
description: A Caspian country where the old stone towers of Baku's Icherisheher quarter stand in the shadow of the futuristic Flame Towers. Oil has been drilled here since the 19th century, and the capital's name is linked to the winds off the Caspian.
fact: Baku is often called the "city of winds" because of the strong, constant gusts blowing in off the Caspian Sea.

name: Kazakhstan
description: The largest country in Central Asia, where endless steppe runs up against the snowy ridges of the Tian Shan. Spacecraft launch from the Baikonur cosmodrome here, and the nomadic traditions of horse breeding are still very much alive.
fact: Kazakhstan is the largest landlocked country in the world.

name: Uzbekistan
description: A country on the ancient Silk Road, where the turquoise domes of the madrasas of Samarkand and Bukhara still hold the memory of the great caravans. Uzbek plov, cooked in a cast-iron kazan, is one of the symbols of the national table.
fact: Samarkand and Bukhara were among the most important hubs on the Silk Road for centuries.

name: Kyrgyzstan
description: A mountain country in the Tian Shan where nomadic life continues: yurts and the high summer pastures known as jailoo are still part of the everyday. Lake Issyk-Kul, one of the largest high-altitude lakes in the world, never freezes in winter.
fact: The name Issyk-Kul means "hot lake" — the water stays unfrozen even in the hardest frosts.

name: Estonia
description: A Baltic country whose capital, Tallinn, has one of the best-preserved medieval old towns in Europe. Estonia is known as a pioneer of digital government and was one of the first countries to offer e-residency.
fact: Estonia was among the first countries in the world to move almost all of its public services online.

name: Latvia
description: A Baltic country of pine forests and sandy beaches, whose capital Riga holds the largest collection of Art Nouveau buildings in Europe. The midsummer festival of Jāņi is celebrated with songs and wreaths of herbs and flowers.
fact: Latvia keeps alive its tradition of national song festivals, where combined choirs of many thousands sing together.

name: Lithuania
description: A Baltic country whose capital Vilnius has the largest medieval old town in Eastern Europe, and which once ruled the vast Grand Duchy of Lithuania. The sand dunes of the Curonian Spit are split between Lithuania and Russia.
fact: Lithuania was the last pagan country in Europe; its people officially adopted Christianity only in the late 14th century.

name: Cyprus
description: A Mediterranean island said in legend to be the birthplace of Aphrodite, goddess of love, who rose from the sea foam off its shore. It is known for ancient mosaics, olive groves and vineyards on the slopes of the Troodos mountains.
fact: Cyprus is famous for halloumi, a cheese that barely melts and so holds its shape beautifully on the grill.

name: Malta
description: A tiny archipelago in the middle of the Mediterranean, ringed by massive fortifications built by the Knights Hospitaller. The honey colour of the local limestone gives Maltese towns a golden glow at sunset.
fact: Malta is one of the most densely populated countries in the world, despite its very modest size.

name: Monaco
description: A tiny state on the French Riviera, famous for the Monte Carlo casino and for the annual Formula 1 race run straight through the city streets. Squeezed between the sea and the hills, it is the second-smallest country in the world after the Vatican.
fact: The Monaco Grand Prix circuit runs along ordinary city streets, including the famous tunnel by the harbour.

name: Vatican City
description: The smallest state in the world, sitting entirely inside Rome and serving as the spiritual centre of the Catholic Church under the Pope. St Peter's Basilica and Michelangelo's ceiling in the Sistine Chapel are its greatest treasures.
fact: The Vatican is so small that you can walk right around it in under an hour.

name: Israel
description: A country on the eastern Mediterranean, holy to three world religions thanks to Jerusalem and its ancient sites. Tel Aviv is known as a busy centre of technology and culture with beaches along the shore.
fact: The Dead Sea on Israel's border is so salty that a swimmer floats on the surface with almost no effort.

name: United Arab Emirates
description: A union of seven emirates on the Persian Gulf that turned desert into futuristic cities like Dubai, with its skyscrapers and artificial islands. Not long ago a modest settlement of fishermen and pearl divers, it is now a global hub for trade and tourism.
fact: Dubai is home to the Burj Khalifa, the tallest building in the world, rising more than eight hundred metres.

name: Saudi Arabia
description: The largest state on the Arabian Peninsula, home to Mecca and Medina, the holiest cities in Islam. The annual hajj pilgrimage brings millions of believers here from all over the world.
fact: Saudi Arabia covers most of the Rub' al Khali, one of the largest sand deserts on the planet.

name: Qatar
description: A small peninsula in the Persian Gulf that grew rich on natural gas and turned its capital, Doha, into a skyline of towers above the desert. In 2022 it hosted the first FIFA World Cup ever held in the Middle East.
fact: Qatar became the first country in the Middle East to host the football World Cup.

name: Iran
description: Heir to the ancient Persian Empire, with the ruins of Persepolis and the lavish turquoise-tiled mosques of Isfahan. The Persian poetry of Hafez and Omar Khayyam and the ritual of tea remain part of everyday culture.
fact: Hand-woven Persian carpets from Iran have been prized among the most valuable in the world for centuries.

name: Jordan
description: A Middle Eastern country where the ancient city of Petra is carved into rose-coloured rock, left behind by the vanished Nabataean civilisation. The Martian landscapes of the Wadi Rum desert are familiar from countless science fiction films.
fact: Petra was cut into the cliffs by the Nabataeans more than two thousand years ago and was long forgotten by the outside world.

name: Egypt
description: The land of the Giza pyramids and the Sphinx, where one of humanity's oldest civilisations grew for millennia along the fertile banks of the Nile. Hieroglyphs, pharaohs and the treasures of Tutankhamun still pull travellers in from everywhere.
fact: The Great Pyramid of Giza remained the tallest structure ever built by people for nearly four thousand years.

name: Morocco
description: A North African country where the maze-like old medinas of Marrakesh and Fez give way to the sands of the Sahara and the slopes of the Atlas mountains. Mint tea, tagine and brightly coloured rugs are part of a rich craft tradition.
fact: Chefchaouen, the blue city in the Moroccan mountains, is painted almost entirely in shades of blue.

name: Tunisia
description: A small North African country holding the ruins of ancient Carthage, which once fought Rome for control of the Mediterranean. Blue-and-white villages like Sidi Bou Said look out over turquoise water from the cliff tops.
fact: The desert scenes of the Star Wars saga were filmed in southern Tunisia.

name: South Africa
description: A country at the southern tip of Africa, where the Atlantic and Indian Oceans meet at Cape Agulhas. Savannah national parks full of lions and elephants and the vineyards near Cape Town reflect a rare range of landscapes.
fact: South Africa has three capitals: administrative Pretoria, legislative Cape Town and judicial Bloemfontein.

name: Kenya
description: An East African country famous for the Maasai Mara savannah, crossed every year by the Great Migration of millions of wildebeest and zebra. Kenyan long-distance runners have dominated the world's marathons for decades.
fact: Kenyan athletes from the Rift Valley region are regarded as some of the strongest marathon runners in the world.

name: Tanzania
description: An East African country that holds Kilimanjaro, the highest mountain in Africa, capped with glacier ice almost on the equator. The Serengeti and the spice island of Zanzibar make it a magnet for travellers.
fact: Kilimanjaro is the tallest free-standing mountain in the world, rising alone rather than as part of a range.

name: Ethiopia
description: One of the oldest independent countries in Africa, never a European colony, with its own calendar and its own alphabet. Ethiopia is considered the birthplace of coffee, and its highland churches at Lalibela are hewn straight out of solid rock.
fact: Legend has it that a goatherd named Kaldi was the first to notice the effect of coffee beans, right here in Ethiopia.

name: Nigeria
description: The most populous country in Africa, with hundreds of ethnic groups and languages, and home to Nollywood, one of the world's biggest film industries by output. Afrobeats and other Nigerian genres now play everywhere.
fact: Many Nollywood films are shot in a matter of weeks and released straight to video, skipping cinemas entirely.

name: Madagascar
description: One of the largest islands on the planet, cut off from the mainland for millions of years, which is why most of its plants and animals live nowhere else. Lemurs and the strange, bottle-shaped baobab trees have become its natural emblems.
fact: More than ninety per cent of lemur species live only on Madagascar and nowhere else in the world.

name: Seychelles
description: An archipelago of more than a hundred islands in the Indian Ocean, famous for the granite boulders on its white beaches and for giant tortoises that live for well over a century. It is one of the least populated countries in the world.
fact: Aldabra Atoll in the Seychelles holds one of the largest populations of giant tortoises in the world.

name: Mauritius
description: An island nation in the Indian Ocean, ringed by coral reefs and known for its blend of Indian, African, European and Chinese cultures. Before Europeans arrived, this was the home of the flightless dodo, now entirely extinct.
fact: Mauritius is the only place the dodo was ever known to live; it was wiped out within decades of the island's discovery.

name: India
description: The most populous country in the world, where hundreds of languages and religions weave together into one vivid culture. The Taj Mahal, spices and Bollywood films are known everywhere, and yoga and meditation began here thousands of years ago.
fact: The Taj Mahal was built as a mausoleum in memory of the beloved wife of the emperor Shah Jahan.

name: Nepal
description: A Himalayan country that holds Everest, the highest point on Earth and a lifelong goal for climbers from all over the world. Buddhist and Hindu temples in Kathmandu sit close to Sherpa villages in the mountain valleys.
fact: Nepal is the only country in the world whose national flag is not rectangular but made of two stacked triangles.

name: Sri Lanka
description: An island nation off the southern tip of India, famous for its hill-country tea plantations and its Indian Ocean beaches. Ancient fortress cities like Sigiriya and centuries-old Buddhist temples keep the island's history close at hand.
fact: Sri Lanka is one of the world's biggest exporters of Ceylon tea, named after the island's former name.

name: Maldives
description: An archipelago of more than a thousand coral islands in the Indian Ocean, now shorthand for luxury holidays in bungalows built over the water. It is the lowest-lying country on Earth, which leaves it badly exposed to rising seas.
fact: Malé, the Maldivian capital, fills almost all of its small island and is one of the most densely built cities in the world.

name: Thailand
description: Southeast Asia at its most colourful: gilded Buddhist temples, the crowded markets of Bangkok and tropical islands like Phuket and Phi Phi. Thai cooking is famous for balancing hot, sour, sweet and salty in a single dish.
fact: Thailand is the only country in Southeast Asia that was never a European colony.

name: Vietnam
description: A country stretched along the South China Sea, with terraced rice fields, the limestone pillars of Ha Long Bay and street food like pho. Vietnamese coffee with condensed milk has become a fixture of local life.
fact: Ha Long Bay, with its thousands of limestone islands, is on UNESCO's World Heritage list.

name: Cambodia
description: A Southeast Asian country where Angkor Wat, the largest religious complex in the world, rises out of the jungle. It was built by the Khmer Empire around a thousand years ago, and the temple even appears on the national flag.
fact: Angkor Wat was originally built as a Hindu temple and later became a Buddhist sanctuary.

name: Malaysia
description: A country split between the Malay Peninsula and the island of Borneo, where the Petronas Twin Towers stand near rainforests among the oldest on the planet. Malaysian food brings Malay, Chinese and Indian cooking together.
fact: The Petronas Towers in Kuala Lumpur are still the tallest twin buildings in the world.

name: Singapore
description: An island city-state off the tip of the Malay Peninsula that went from modest port to global financial centre in half a century. Gardens by the Bay, with its giant artificial supertrees, has become the emblem of the modern city.
fact: Singapore is one of the few city-states in the modern world, alongside Monaco and the Vatican.

name: Indonesia
description: The largest archipelago on the planet, spread across more than seventeen thousand islands between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Bali, with its rice terraces and Hindu temples, is the destination travellers know best.
fact: Indonesia is the largest island nation on Earth and one of the most populous countries in the world.

name: Philippines
description: An archipelago of more than seven thousand islands in Southeast Asia, holding dozens of languages and cultural traditions. The white beaches of Boracay and the Banaue rice terraces, carved into the mountains entirely by hand, are its natural pride.
fact: Local farmers have worked the Banaue rice terraces on Luzon by hand for centuries, keeping an ancient irrigation system alive.

name: South Korea
description: An East Asian country that went from poverty to technological leadership in a few decades and gave the world K-pop and Korean cinema. Spicy kimchi and Seoul street food have become part of global pop culture.
fact: South Korea is one of the world leaders in internet speed and in overall technological development.

name: North Korea
description: A state in the north of the Korean Peninsula, with mountain ranges, pine forests and the volcano of Paektu near its northern border. Pyongyang, the capital, is known for its wide avenues and monumental mid-20th-century architecture.
fact: Naengmyeon, a cold buckwheat noodle dish served in icy broth, is considered the signature food of Pyongyang.

name: Mongolia
description: A country of endless steppe between Russia and China, where herding and life in felt yurts are still everyday reality for many families. This is where Genghis Khan set out in the 13th century to build the largest land empire in history.
fact: Mongolia is one of the least densely populated countries in the world, with only a few million people across a huge territory.

name: Australia
description: A country that is also a continent, with wildlife found nowhere else and the Great Barrier Reef, the largest coral system on the planet, off its coast. The Sydney Opera House and its sail-like roof is one of the most recognisable buildings anywhere.
fact: Most Australian animals, kangaroos and koalas included, are not found in the wild anywhere else in the world.

name: New Zealand
description: An island country of green hills, fjords and volcanoes that served as the location for The Lord of the Rings trilogy. The culture of the Māori, including the haka, remains a living part of national identity.
fact: For a long stretch of its history, New Zealand had several times more sheep than people.

name: Fiji
description: An archipelago of more than three hundred tropical islands in the South Pacific, famous for its coral reefs and the warmth of its people. For such a small country, Fiji fields one of the strongest rugby sevens teams in the world.
fact: Fiji's rugby sevens gold at the 2016 Olympics was the country's first Olympic medal of any colour.

name: Canada
description: The second-largest country in the world, running from the Atlantic to the Pacific, with vast forests, lakes and the Rocky Mountains. The maple leaf on the flag and ice hockey have long been national symbols.
fact: Canada has the longest coastline of any country in the world.

name: Mexico
description: The land of the ancient Maya and Aztecs, whose pyramids still rise out of the jungle and the desert. Mexican cuisine, with its tequila, tacos and fiery salsas, is recognised by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage.
fact: The Day of the Dead in Mexico is not about grief but about joyfully remembering relatives who have died.

name: Cuba
description: The largest island in the Caribbean, famous for the 1950s cars still rolling through the streets of Havana and for the rhythms of salsa and rumba. Cuban rum and cigars are considered among the finest in the world.
fact: Cuban cigars are rolled by hand, and the best tobacco for them grows in the western Vuelta Abajo valley.

name: Jamaica
description: A Caribbean island that gave the world reggae and Bob Marley, along with sprinters who have owned the Olympic track for decades. White-sand beaches and the Blue Mountains, with their famous coffee plantations, draw visitors from everywhere.
fact: Jamaican sprinters, Usain Bolt among them, set world records in athletics for years on end.

name: Dominican Republic
description: A Caribbean country sharing the island of Hispaniola with Haiti, with the white beaches of Punta Cana and the driving rhythms of merengue and bachata. Santo Domingo is considered the oldest continuously inhabited European-founded city in the Americas.
fact: Bachata, born in the Dominican countryside, eventually grew into a dance genre popular all over the world.

name: The Bahamas
description: An archipelago of some seven hundred islands and cays in the Atlantic near Florida, famous for turquoise water and coral reefs. By the generally accepted account, this is where Christopher Columbus first came ashore in 1492.
fact: The Bahamas are known for their blue holes, deep underwater sinkholes in the limestone that attract divers from all over.

name: Costa Rica
description: A Central American country that abolished its standing army and put the money into protecting rainforest, which shelters an enormous variety of plants and animals. Volcanoes, cloud forest and beaches on two oceans make it a magnet for ecotourism.
fact: Almost all of Costa Rica's electricity comes from renewable sources: hydropower, volcanic heat and wind.

name: Panama
description: A narrow isthmus between the two Americas, cut through by the Panama Canal, one of the most important artificial waterways in world trade. The towers of Panama City stand close to dense rainforest and the lands of the indigenous Guna.
fact: The Panama Canal links the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans and handles dozens of ships every day.

name: Brazil
description: The largest country in South America, holding most of the Amazon, the biggest rainforest on the planet. Carnival in Rio de Janeiro, football and the statue of Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado are instantly recognisable.
fact: Brazil is the only Portuguese-speaking country in South America, a legacy of its colonial past.

name: Argentina
description: The land of tango, of the endless pampas and its gaucho herdsmen, and of the snowy peaks of Patagonia in the far south. Argentine beef and the football that produced Maradona and Messi are matters of national pride.
fact: The Perito Moreno glacier in Patagonia drops huge blocks of ice into the lake with a roar, right in front of onlookers.

name: Chile
description: A narrow ribbon of a country along the Pacific coast, taking in the Atacama Desert, one of the driest places on Earth, and the snowy summits of the Andes. Chilean vineyards produce some of the best wine in the southern hemisphere.
fact: Chile stretches nearly four and a half thousand kilometres from north to south while staying remarkably narrow.

name: Peru
description: An Andean country that keeps the ruins of Machu Picchu, the lost Inca city high in the mountains and one of the new wonders of the world. Peruvian cooking, mixing native and immigrant traditions, is among the most varied anywhere.
fact: Machu Picchu was built by the Incas in the 15th century and stayed unknown to the outside world until the early 20th.

name: Venezuela
description: A country in northern South America, home to Angel Falls, the tallest waterfall in the world, dropping from a tabletop mountain straight into the jungle. A Caribbean coast and the snowy Andes sit beside the vast plains of the llanos.
fact: Angel Falls is nearly twenty times taller than Niagara and is considered the highest waterfall on the planet.

name: Bolivia
description: A country in the heart of the Andes, home to the Salar de Uyuni, the largest salt flat in the world, which turns into a vast mirror after the rains. La Paz, the seat of government, is one of the highest capitals on Earth.
fact: La Paz sits so high and on such steep slopes that a network of cable cars has taken over part of its public transport.

name: Uruguay
description: A small country on the Atlantic coast between Argentina and Brazil, where football is close to a religion and the very first World Cup was held in 1930. Uruguayans are among the world's most devoted drinkers of yerba mate.
fact: Uruguay both hosted and won the very first football World Cup in 1930.

name: Colombia
description: The source of famous high-altitude arabica coffee and of the world's main emerald deposits, mined here for centuries. Pacific and Caribbean coasts, snow-capped Andean peaks and vast flower farms make for a startlingly varied landscape.
fact: Colombia is the only country in South America with coastlines on both the Pacific and the Atlantic.

name: Ecuador
description: The country takes its name from the equator, which crosses its northern part. In a small area it packs the snowy volcanoes of the Andes, Amazon rainforest and the Galápagos Islands with their singular wildlife.
fact: The Galápagos Islands, which belong to Ecuador, gave Charles Darwin the ideas behind his theory of evolution.

name: Paraguay
description: One of the two landlocked countries in South America, rich instead in fresh water and hydroelectric power. Guaraní is still widely spoken here, used alongside Spanish in everyday life.
fact: Guaraní is one of the few indigenous languages of the Americas to hold official status alongside Spanish.

name: Guatemala
description: The land of the Maya, holding some of the most impressive ruins of that civilisation deep in dense rainforest. Volcanoes, coffee plantations and the bright woven textiles of indigenous communities shape modern Guatemala.
fact: The ancient Maya city of Tikal, hidden in the Guatemalan jungle, lay buried under vegetation for centuries.

name: Honduras
description: A country with long coral reefs off its Caribbean shore and dense tropical rainforest further inland. It also holds Copán, one of the most important cities of the ancient Maya civilisation, famous for its carved stone inscriptions.
fact: The barrier reef off Honduras is part of the second-largest coral system in the world, after the Great Barrier Reef.

name: El Salvador
description: The smallest country in mainland America by area, but with dozens of volcanoes and a Pacific coast that surfers know well. Pupusas, thick stuffed corn flatbreads, are the staple of the local kitchen and eaten almost daily.
fact: El Salvador is the only country in Central America with no coastline on the Caribbean Sea.

name: Nicaragua
description: A country of lakes and volcanoes: Lake Nicaragua, the largest in Central America, is home to freshwater bull sharks, a rarity in an inland body of water. The colonial architecture of Granada and León stands near active volcanoes.
fact: Lake Nicaragua holds the island of Ometepe, formed by two volcanoes joined by a narrow strip of land.

name: Haiti
description: The first independent Black republic in the world, born of a slave uprising in the early 19th century. It shares the island of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic and is known for its vivid naive painting and the rhythms of compas.
fact: The name Haiti comes from the language of the Taíno, the island's indigenous people, and is translated as "mountainous land".

name: Trinidad and Tobago
description: The birthplace of the steel pan and of calypso, the carnival music that seeded a whole family of Caribbean genres. Tobago is known for its coral reefs, Trinidad for its oil industry and its riotous carnival.
fact: Trinidad holds Pitch Lake, the largest natural deposit of asphalt in the world.

name: Barbados
description: A small coral island, the easternmost of the Lesser Antilles chain, lying out in Atlantic waters. Rum in its modern form was born here, and the pale sandy beaches draw visitors from all over the world.
fact: Barbados is considered the place where rum was first produced on an industrial scale.

name: Slovakia
description: A mountainous country in the very heart of Europe, where the Tatras pair Alpine scenery with wooden towns and castles perched on crags. In Bratislava, the capital on the Danube, Austrian, Hungarian and Slavic influences still mingle.
fact: Slovakia has kept more than a hundred castles and fortresses, a remarkable number for such a small territory.

name: Luxembourg
description: One of the smallest countries in Europe and at the same time a global financial centre with one of the highest incomes per head anywhere. In the tiny capital, medieval fortress walls stand beside the glass towers of the banks.
fact: Tens of thousands of people commute into Luxembourg for work every day from neighbouring France, Germany and Belgium.

name: Liechtenstein
description: A tiny Alpine principality between Switzerland and Austria, still ruled by a hereditary monarchy. Ski slopes, a medieval castle above the capital and one of the highest GDPs per head in the world keep it on the map despite its size.
fact: Liechtenstein is one of the few countries in the world with no airport offering scheduled flights.

name: Andorra
description: A state wedged into the Pyrenees between Spain and France, governed for centuries by two co-princes, one French and one Spanish. Today it is known for its ski resorts and duty-free shopping, which pull in visitors from across Europe.
fact: Andorra's heads of state are formally the president of France and the Spanish bishop of Urgell, serving jointly.

name: San Marino
description: One of the oldest republics in the world, set on the slopes of Mount Titano among the hills of Italy, which surrounds the tiny country completely. The three medieval towers above the capital are its emblem and a UNESCO site.
fact: By tradition San Marino was founded in the 4th century, making it one of the oldest states still in existence.

name: Albania
description: A mountainous Balkan country with a long Adriatic and Ionian coast that gets compared these days to pricier Mediterranean resorts. Decades of isolation left a visible mark on the landscape: thousands of small concrete bunkers are scattered across it.
fact: Thousands of concrete bunkers built in the second half of the 20th century still stand all across Albania.

name: North Macedonia
description: A small Balkan country around Skopje, once crossed by important trade routes between Europe and Asia. Classical antiquity sits alongside Ottoman architecture and picturesque mountain lakes, Lake Ohrid among them.
fact: Lake Ohrid, on the border of North Macedonia and Albania, is one of the oldest lakes in Europe, several million years old.

name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
description: A Balkan country where Ottoman, Austro-Hungarian and Slavic heritage meet, most visibly in Sarajevo and Mostar. Mountain rivers, canyons and old stone bridges give its landscape a look all its own.
fact: The Stari Most bridge in Mostar, protected by UNESCO, is a fine example of 16th-century Ottoman engineering.

name: Moldova
description: A small country between Romania and Ukraine, known for its fertile soil and long winemaking tradition. The Moldovan wine cellars of Cricova and Mileștii Mici are among the largest wine stores on the planet.
fact: The underground tunnels of the Mileștii Mici winery in Moldova hold one of the biggest wine collections in the world.

name: Pakistan
description: A country at the foot of the Karakoram and the Himalayas, with several of the highest peaks on the planet, K2 included. The Indus Valley cradled one of the world's oldest civilisations; today Pakistan is known for fierce spices and open hospitality.
fact: K2, on Pakistani territory, is the second-highest mountain on Earth after Everest.

name: Bangladesh
description: A country built on the delta of the Ganges and the Brahmaputra, laced with channels and rice paddies, and one of the most densely populated in the world. In the south lies the Sundarbans, the largest mangrove forest anywhere, home to Bengal tigers.
fact: Bangladesh is almost entirely surrounded by India, with only a short border with Myanmar in the southeast.

name: Afghanistan
description: A mountain country at the crossroads of the old Silk Road trade routes, where Persian, Indian and Central Asian cultures mixed for centuries. The Minaret of Jam and the Blue Mosque in Mazar-i-Sharif are among the region's most significant monuments.
fact: Lapis lazuli has been mined in Afghan Badakhshan for thousands of years; the blue stone reached ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia.

name: Iraq
description: The land between the Tigris and the Euphrates, known as Mesopotamia, where some of the first cities and the first writing appeared. The legacy of Sumer, Babylon and Akkad makes this one of the key territories in the history of civilisation.
fact: Cuneiform, one of the oldest writing systems in the world, arose in Mesopotamia, in what is now Iraq.

name: Syria
description: Home to one of the oldest continuously inhabited capitals in the world: Damascus appears in written records going back several thousand years. Trade routes linking the Mediterranean with Mesopotamia and Arabia have crossed the country since antiquity.
fact: The Syrian capital gave its name to damask, the patterned fabric, and to Damascus steel.

name: Lebanon
description: A small country on the eastern Mediterranean shore whose mountain cedars were once used by the Phoenicians to build ships and appear in ancient texts. Beirut served for centuries as a crossroads of trade and culture in the region.
fact: The Lebanon cedar, which grows in the country's mountains, appears on the national flag.

name: Yemen
description: A country in the south of the Arabian Peninsula with multi-storey houses of mud brick; the old town of Shibam earned the nickname "Manhattan of the desert" for those towers. The island of Socotra offshore is famous for plants found nowhere else on Earth.
fact: Socotra, part of Yemen, grows the dragon blood tree with its distinctive umbrella crown, found nowhere else.

name: Kuwait
description: A small state at the northern end of the Persian Gulf, one of the wealthiest in the world thanks to oil discovered in the mid-20th century. Before the oil era, Kuwait was known as a centre of pearl diving and maritime trade.
fact: The country's name comes from the Arabic word "kut", used for a small fortress by the water.

name: Bahrain
description: An island state in the Persian Gulf, among the first in the region to start pumping oil, back in the 1930s. Bahrain is also known for the ancient Dilmun burial mounds and for a Formula 1 circuit that has hosted races since the mid-2000s.
fact: The King Fahd Causeway, about twenty-five kilometres long, links Bahrain to Saudi Arabia.

name: Oman
description: A country in the southeast of the Arabian Peninsula with some of the most varied landscapes in the region, from desert to the green heights of Jebel Akhdar. For centuries Oman was a hub of the incense trade, above all frankincense, still harvested here.
fact: Frankincense, exported from Oman across the world for centuries, is still tapped from boswellia trees the traditional way.

name: Myanmar
description: A Southeast Asian country where thousands of Buddhist temples and stupas, built in the Middle Ages, stand across the plain of Bagan. The golden Shwedagon Pagoda in Yangon is one of the most venerated Buddhist sites in the region.
fact: Myanmar's capital Naypyidaw was built almost from scratch and only became the country's principal city in the mid-2000s.

name: Laos
description: A landlocked Southeast Asian country where the Buddhist temples of Luang Prabang sit near the Bolaven Plateau and the mysterious Plain of Jars. The dawn alms-giving to monks in Luang Prabang is one of its most recognisable traditions.
fact: The origin of the thousands of stone jars on the Plain of Jars in Laos, some thousands of years old, is still unexplained.

name: Bhutan
description: A Himalayan kingdom known for measuring success not only by gross domestic product but by an index of Gross National Happiness. The Taktsang monastery, clinging to a sheer cliff face, is one of the most recognisable Buddhist temples in the world.
fact: Bhutan only legalised television in the late 1990s, among the last countries in the world to do so.

name: Uganda
description: An East African country Winston Churchill called the "pearl of Africa" for the range of its landscapes, from the source of the Nile to mountain forests inhabited by gorillas. Its national parks are one of the few places on Earth to see gorillas in the wild.
fact: Part of Lake Victoria, the largest lake in Africa, lies within Uganda, and the Nile flowing out of it begins its journey here.

name: Algeria
description: The largest country in Africa by area, most of it taken up by the Sahara with its dunes and rock paintings thousands of years old. In the north stand the striking ruins of the Roman city of Timgad.
fact: The rock art of the Tassili n'Ajjer plateau in Algeria, several thousand years old, is on UNESCO's World Heritage list.

name: Libya
description: A country on the Mediterranean coast of North Africa, with the Sahara covering most of its territory. The ruins of the ancient cities of Leptis Magna and Sabratha are among the best-preserved Roman sites on the African continent.
fact: Leptis Magna, once one of the largest Roman cities in Africa, is still striking for how well its buildings survive.

name: Sudan
description: A country in northeast Africa where the White and Blue Nile merge into a single river at Khartoum. Sudan holds more pyramids than Egypt does, built by the rulers of the ancient kingdom of Kush.
fact: About three thousand years ago the Nubian rulers of Kush conquered Egypt too, forming one of its dynasties.

name: Ghana
description: A West African country named after a medieval empire, though its territory lies south of that state's historic lands. Ghana is a major cocoa producer, and old European forts built for trade still stand along its coast.
fact: In 1957 Ghana became the first country in sub-Saharan Africa to win independence from colonial rule.

name: Senegal
description: The westernmost point of mainland Africa, where Dakar faces out into the Atlantic. Gorée Island off the Senegalese coast, with its old buildings, is on UNESCO's World Heritage list as a historic site.
fact: Senegal is famous for laamb, a traditional form of wrestling that fills stadiums with thousands of spectators.

name: Zimbabwe
description: A country in southern Africa named after the ancient stone city of Great Zimbabwe, built from carefully fitted blocks without any mortar. On the border with Zambia is Victoria Falls, one of the widest sheets of falling water in the world.
fact: In the local language Victoria Falls is called Mosi-oa-Tunya, "the smoke that thunders".

name: Ivory Coast
description: A West African country whose name means exactly what it says: European traders called this stretch of shore the Ivory Coast. Abidjan, its largest city, is regarded as one of the most dynamic economic centres in the region.
fact: Ivory Coast is the world's largest producer of cocoa beans, supplying a substantial share of the global harvest.
